besluite.rede: A 'soos' comparison placed after the verb cluster is normal Afrikaans; the reorder is lateral.
'daarby in' is ordinary recipe Afrikaans and carries the sense of adding to the water; 'daarin' drops that and is no clearer.

besluite.fout: The nominalised subject 'Die roer' is stiff, and a Grade 5 reader may first read 'roer' as the noun (rudder, gun).
besluite.rede: The verbal construction reads naturally and keeps the same claim that stirring turns the two into one lump-free paste.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.
besluite.rede: Both clauses have their own subject and verb ('Die pap bly', 'dit word'), so AWS 2017 requires the comma.
Afrikaans commonly writes stacked adjectives without a comma, and the lesson already writes 'droë wit poeier' without one; the comma is lateral and inconsistent.

besluite.fout: 'gaan tussen planke' leaves the movement unfinished, and the AWS comma before the clause-joining 'en' is missing.
besluite.rede: 'tussen planke in' completes the movement without changing where the paste goes, and both clauses have their own subject and verb, so the comma belongs.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma; the clause 'en' runs straight on from the list 'en'.
besluite.rede: The comma marks the second clause ('dit loop') and separates it from 'droog en los', where no comma belongs.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma between the imperative clause and 'jy kry'; 'by en jy' can make a reader stumble.
besluite.rede: Two main clauses, the second with its own subject and verb; the comma also stops 'by' being read with what follows.
'Die pasta is' and 'dit plak' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: The nominalised subject 'Die meng alleen' is wooden.
besluite.rede: 'Net deur te meng' can be read as 'only by mixing' (mixing is the only way to get glue) rather than 'mixing alone is enough', so the fix needs other wording.
'Die los meel verdwyn' and ''n mens hou' each have their own subject and verb.
Both clauses have their own subject and verb, and the protected word 'hitte' stays as it is.
'Iemand roer' and 'die korrels los op' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma between the imperative clause and a clause with its own subject and verb.
besluite.rede: Two main clauses are joined by 'en', so the comma follows the AWS rule and matches comma 8.
'Nat klei is' and ''n mens kan vorm' each have their own subject and verb.
'hy' for a concrete object such as a brick is standard Afrikaans, the lesson uses 'sy' for the jelly elsewhere, and 'dit' in the sentence before already refers to the clay.
'Party kleibakstene word' and 'ander word' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma after 'nie' before clause-joining 'en'.
besluite.rede: Both clauses have their own subject and verb, and the comma makes the double-negative close easier to read.

besluite.fout: 'na die tyd' is a loose, English-coloured expression.
besluite.rede: Straight after the sentence about comparing properties, 'daarna' could read as 'after comparing' instead of 'after the mixing', so the fault needs wording that keeps the time reference clear.
Set against 'voor', the temporal 'na' is already clear, so AWS does not call for the accent, and the lesson writes 'na' without one elsewhere.
